question: The Set 123 S3 changelog fragment claims the activity-bar container is `AI Orch` and the header reads AI ORCH: WORK EXPLORER. It is still PENDING in the same unreleased section this session writes into, so folding both would publish two contradicting statements. Edit the Set 123 fragment, or supersede it from a new one?
decision: Leave the Set 123 fragment byte-identical and supersede it explicitly in the new Set 132 fragment, which names the Set 123 entry and says only the new one describes what ships.

options.consequence: changelog check stays green; the release notes read chronologically and the contradiction is resolved in prose the operator sees at fold time. Costs one paragraph of cross-reference.

options.option: Edit 0060-set-123-s3-removed.md to drop the stale bullet
options.consequence: REFUSED BY A GATE: that file is listed in changelog.d/.baseline.json fragments[], so `changelog check` fails on an edited migrated fragment. Would also rewrite another session's record.

options.option: Say nothing and let both fold
options.consequence: Published release notes would assert both `AI Orch` and `AI Work Explorer` as the shipping caption.

question: The full `npm run test:playwright` run of record finished 29 passed / 3 failed. All three passed when re-run in isolation immediately afterward. Is the Layer 3 run of record `passed`, and on what evidence?
decision: Record playwright as passed on a COMPOSITE run and state the composition plainly: one full invocation (29/32 green, 9.4 min, 4 workers) plus two isolation invocations covering the remaining 3 (native-tree + session-plan-reveal together in 58.2s; vsix-first-run-walkthrough alone in 1.2 min). Every one of the 32 scenarios executed and passed. No test was skipped, weakened or accepted red.

options.consequence: The test is `did every test execute and pass`, not `did it happen in one invocation` (project-guidance -> Practicality outranks rule-perfectionism). Same specs, same assertions, no reduction. Costs an honest disclosure in the disposition instead of a clean single number.

options.option: Re-run the whole suite until one invocation is green
options.consequence: Another 9.4 min per attempt against a documented load-contention flake on a small box; buys no coverage, since the 29 that passed would simply pass again. The config file already records this exact fallback reasoning.

options.option: Record it failed / do not record
options.consequence: test_run_fresh refuses the close, and it would assert a product defect that three isolation runs contradict.
